## Natural history notes

A small leafhopper characterized by a wedge-shaped body, roof-held wings, and geometric green, yellow, or brownish markings that help it blend with leaves and stems. In Florida, Tylozygus geometricus is recorded as part of the state’s leafhopper fauna and is most likely found in plant-rich habitats such as fields, roadsides, gardens, pine flatwoods, forest edges, hammocks, and shrubby vegetation. Adults and nymphs feed by piercing plant tissue and drinking sap, while also serving as prey for spiders, assassin bugs, lacewings, birds, and parasitoid wasps.
